clue.text: Revisited Sumerian land

indicators.note: revisited suggests going over something again in a new form, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A historian returns to the ancient realm of the Sumerians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sumerian land' looks like Sumer itself; 'Revisited' is the anagram signal working on SUMERIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Suriname is a country on the north coast of South America, so a land.

clue.text: Young lady wanting head, veiled in part

definitions.text: Young lady wanting head, veiled in part

parts.words: Young lady wanting head, veiled in part
parts.note: the biblical princess danced the dance of the seven veils and demanded John the Baptist's head as her reward

explanation.surface: A girl wanting to be in charge is half hidden behind a veil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting head' suggests a missing first letter, but it means she wanted a severed head.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod's stepdaughter danced veiled and asked for the Baptist's head on a platter.

clue.text: Consider changing gear en route

indicators.note: changing means altering the order, so the letters of gear are reshuffled

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a route

explanation.surface: A cyclist thinks about switching gears while on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it carefully and think about it.

clue.text: Marilyn once bared all? That's 27

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer to 27 across, a word for ordinary

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe was born Norma Jeane

indicators.note: bared means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of all are removed

explanation.surface: Marilyn Monroe once posed nude; that was quite usual for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bared all' suggests nudity, but it strips the ends from ALL to leave L.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual or typical, the same as the ordinary sense of 27 across.

clue.text: Underground cave men dig path up

indicators.note: up here means in disorder, so the letters of men dig path are mixed

explanation.surface: Cave dwellers excavate a path upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' is Latin for beware, so 'Underground cave' is the London Underground's warning; it is not a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the famous platform warning on the London Tube, telling passengers to beware.

clue.text: British gangster stole capital from Panama

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL
a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

explanation.surface: A British crook makes off with money taken from Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' reads as a verb but is the noun, a wrap; 'capital' means money, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The balboa is the currency of Panama, so money or capital from there.

clue.text: A saucy virgin doesn't open mouth

parts.note: pert means cheeky, saucy

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter is missing

parts.note: pure means chaste, virgin

explanation.surface: A cheeky innocent stays tight-lipped.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening, such as the mouth of a cave or a tube.

clue.text: A youngest son from African country going round block

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the country is placed around the block

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
a jam is a blockage

explanation.surface: A young man from Africa walks around the block.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin was Jacob's youngest son, so the name is used for any youngest son.

clue.text: The number whose logarithm is y produces a contradiction

parts.note: an antilog is the number whose logarithm is a given value

explanation.surface: A mathematician's definition turns out to contradict itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The antilog of y is exactly the number whose logarithm is y, so the long phrase gives ANTILOG followed by Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Antilogy is a rare term for a contradiction in terms or ideas.

clue.text: Organised religions? I dispensed with such restraints

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters of religions are rearranged
dispensed with means done without, so the letter I is dropped from that pool

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether organised religion is a kind of shackle best thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: RELIGIONS has nine letters; taking out one I leaves eight to rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg irons are shackles fitted to the ankles, the restraints the clue imagines religion to be.

clue.text: Fish European Parliament rejected as a food item

indicators.note: rejected is taken as thrown back, so the fish and the parliament are read backwards together

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: MEPs vote down a proposal about fish as a foodstuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a legume eaten as a snack, so an item of food.

clue.text: Napoleon of crime affected by opinion pollsters

parts.note: MORI is a British market research and polling company
arty means pretentiously artistic, affected

explanation.surface: A dictator of the underworld is swayed by what the polls say.
explanation.walkthrough: MORI is a well-known British polling firm. Sherlock Holmes calls Professor Moriarty 'the Napoleon of crime'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's arch-villain is described by Holmes as the Napoleon of crime.

clue.text: Letter-writer makes typo oddly when entering his other name

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the picked letters go inside the other name

parts.note: the apostle was Saul of Tarsus before his conversion

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of typo

explanation.surface: A correspondent slips up in a strange way while typing his alternative name.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostle was known as Saul before his conversion; he wrote many of the New Testament epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle wrote the Pauline epistles, the letters to early churches in the New Testament.

clue.text: Sad song writer has kebab brought over during this time

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the reversed kebab sits within the words for this time
brought over means turned over, so the kebab word is read backwards

parts.note: a doner is a kind of kebab

explanation.surface: A composer of laments has a takeaway delivered at this hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or dirge, so a threnodist composes mournful songs.

clue.text: A swimmer smoked something to divert the attention

definitions.meaning: a kipper-like fish cured by smoking until it turns reddish
a false clue laid to lead people off the scent

explanation.surface: A fish was cured over smoke to throw someone off the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured fish dragged across a trail was said to throw hounds off the scent, hence a distraction.

clue.text: Maiden I whipped is in spanking condition

indicators.note: whipped is taken as snatched away, so the letter I is removed

parts.note: a maiden is an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A young woman was beaten, yet emerges looking fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped' and 'spanking' set a corporal-punishment scene; 'whipped' means removed, and 'spanking' means splendidly new.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarred means unblemished, and spanking condition is pristine, like-new condition.

clue.text: Folksy song by Buddy Holly? That's 27

definitions.meaning: the title of Buddy Holly's gentle 1957 song
the cross-reference stands for the answer to 27 across, meaning ordinary

explanation.surface: A homespun Buddy Holly number counts as a classic tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means commonplace or routine, which is the ordinary sense of 27 across.

clue.text: Chemical compound, say, receiving attention

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for say holds the word for attention

parts.note: to state is to say
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A chemist announces a compound and is listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A stearate is a salt or ester of stearic acid, a chemical compound.

clue.text: They're starting on about going to Mars

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word on is read backwards

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or vitiate, so mars gives vitiates

explanation.surface: Astronauts are setting off on a voyage to the red planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet but is the verb, spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Novitiates are novices, people just beginning in a religious order.

clue.text: English saint shaves head inside

indicators.note: shaving the head removes the first letter

parts.note: St Swithin was a ninth-century Bishop of Winchester

explanation.surface: An English holy man has his head shaved indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: St Swithin's Day in Britain is linked with the folklore that rain on that day means forty more days of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Within means inside, as in staying within the walls.

clue.text: Had trouble with each rising flower

indicators.note: each rising says both pieces go upwards in this down clue, so they are read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone struggled with every bloom that came up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, HAD gives DAH and AIL gives LIA, the two together making the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden plant grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Skilled in metrical patterns?

definitions.meaning: practised or knowledgeable, as when well-informed in a subject
written as poetry, in lines with regular metre

explanation.surface: Accomplished at writing poetic forms.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well grounded in a subject is to be expert; and text put into poetic lines has been made into poetry.

clue.text: Article written by US woman overseas

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by an American woman reporting from foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in a foreign country, across the sea.

clue.text: Party that's popular in China could get to rule

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so the word for popular goes into the word for China

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A political party that is popular in China may come to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate meaning mate, a friend; it is not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control or hold sway over, to rule.

clue.text: King raced around racecourse

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters about, so raced is rearranged

explanation.surface: The monarch drove a lap of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in North Yorkshire with a horse-racing course.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar in North Yorkshire is home to a well-known flat racing track.

clue.text: Parsons maybe going commando when preaching

indicators.note: preaching is speaking out from the pulpit, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: going commando is slang for wearing no underwear, being knickerless

explanation.surface: A clergyman wears nothing under his robes while giving his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parsons' looks like clergy but is the surname of Nicholas Parsons, long-time host of BBC radio's Just a Minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Parsons was a British broadcaster, so a first name going with that surname.

clue.text: Poet laureate on the wagon train finally crosses Delaware

indicators.note: crosses here means goes over to the far side of, so the final letter lands after Delaware

parts.note: being on the wagon means abstaining from alcohol, dry
DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of train

explanation.surface: A sober poet rides a wagon train over the Delaware River.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' and 'train' together suggest pioneers, but the first is teetotal and only the last letter of train is used.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the first official English Poet Laureate, appointed in 1668.

clue.text: Ordinary song

definitions.meaning: a well-established tune regularly performed, as in a jazz repertoire

explanation.surface: An unremarkable tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means usual, and a standard is a classic song often covered by performers.
